description: Agent Limits: submit a limit set with its breach behavior: for each limit, what hitting it does to the work (stop, escalate, queue or continue), who an escalation goes to and whether that is a named person, a role, a channel or another agent, how long they have to answer, what happens when no one answers (deny, allow or keep waiting), who clears queued work, when the breach path was written down and when the limit was first hit. The signed report follows each breach to its end and names every limit with no written path, every limit the work continues past, every escalation to no one or that goes through on silence, every escalation to an agent, role or channel rather than a named person or with no time to answer, every queue nobody clears, and every path written down after the first breach, with the fix for each. This reads where the work goes at the wall: whether a cap design names a breach rule at all is wever_exposure-cap-check and when an escalation fires and moves to the next owner is wever_escalation-threshold-check. Verdict wall_not_held, breach_path_gaps, breach_path_unverified or breach_paths_defined. POST /api/breach-path-check. Reads only the material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, sharing, configuration change or external write. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-limits-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-limits/.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

limits.description: Each limit with its breach behavior.

on_breach.description: What hitting the limit does to the work: stop it, escalate it, queue it or let it continue.

on_silence.description: What happens when the recipient does not answer in time.

response_time.description: How long the recipient has to answer, such as 30 minutes.
